To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) ODIN like methods can detect OoD data without tuning with Oo D data; (2) the difficulty of detecting Oo D data is significantly affected by whether the data distribution shift is semantic or not; (3) the proposed decomposition of confidence scoring can help in detection performance; (4) the proposed modified pre processing method can help in detection as well.

(1) ODIN like methods, which are based on input pre processing, can be used without training on OoD data and still perform better than other methods that do not use input pre processing; (2) ODIN like strategies can work well for non semantic distribution shifts, but fail to work well for semantic distribution shifts; and (3) the performance of OoD detection methods can be significantly affected by the type of distribution shift present in the data.

1) we propose two strategies for improving the performance of ODIN like methods that do not need OoD data for training or tuning; 2) we analyze the difference between semantic and non semantic distribution shifts and show the limitations of the ODIN like methods; 3) we show that the two strategies can improve the performance of a baseline OoD detector on a large scale dataset by a large margin.
